Life insurance for veterans: VA coverage and private options

Veterans can have life insurance through the VA, a private policy, or both. Which costs less depends on your age, your health, and how long you need it. We lay the options side by side.

Reviewed by Luay Sadqi, Licensed Agent · NPN 21370662 · Updated November 2026

What the VA offers

The Department of Veterans Affairs runs several life insurance programs, including these three. The deadline table below covers the others.

  • SGLI (Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance) is group term coverage of up to $500,000 while you serve.
  • VGLI (Veterans' Group Life Insurance) lets you keep term coverage after you separate, from $10,000 up to the amount of SGLI you had, with a $500,000 limit. The monthly cost depends only on your age and the amount, and it goes up with each older age band. Coverage lasts for life as long as you pay the premiums. The deadlines to apply are in the table below.
  • VALife is guaranteed-acceptance whole life of up to $40,000, in $10,000 steps, for veterans age 80 or under with a service-connected disability rating, even 0%. You do not need to prove good health. Full coverage starts 2 years after you apply. If death happens during that wait, your beneficiaries get the premiums paid plus interest.

Program rules and rates are set by the VA and can change. Check the details at VA.gov life insurance before you decide.

VA deadlines after you leave the military

These dates come from VA.gov and can change, so check the linked VA page before you act. Still serving? Keep your SGLI. The dates below count from the day you leave the military.

When private coverage is worth comparing

  • You are in good health. VGLI's monthly cost depends only on your age and the amount, so your health does not change it. A private policy is priced on your health, age and tobacco use, so it can come out higher or lower. We quote both so you can compare.
  • You want a level premium. Level term is built to keep the same premium for the term you choose, such as 10, 20 or 30 years. Check the policy for what is guaranteed. VGLI's rate goes up each time you move into an older age band on VA's rate table.
  • You need more than $500,000. A mortgage, young children, or a business can call for more than the VA maximum.
  • You have a mortgage but no Specially Adapted Housing grant. VMLI, in the table above, requires that grant. A private option is mortgage protection insurance, which is usually term life you own, sized to the balance and the years left.
  • You want permanent coverage beyond $40,000. Whole life or guaranteed universal life can cover what VALife does not.
  • You want coverage for a spouse. VGLI and VALife insure the veteran. A spouse with FSGLI coverage can convert it to a permanent individual policy within 120 days of your separation. A private policy can cover a spouse in their own name.
When VA coverage may fit better: If you have serious health conditions, VGLI applied for within 240 days of leaving does not ask you to prove good health, and VALife accepts veterans 80 or younger with a service-connected rating. VA warns that if you wait and a private company turns you down, you may miss the 240-day window (VA.gov, updated Nov 3, 2026). We will tell you when VA coverage looks like the better fit.

Final expense for veterans

VA burial allowances can help pay some burial, funeral and plot costs when a veteran meets VA’s rules. VA sets who qualifies and how much it pays; see VA.gov burial allowances (updated Oct 30, 2026). If your family wants more set aside, a small final expense policy can sit alongside VA burial benefits and VALife. Guaranteed-issue final expense policies have a waiting period or a graded benefit in the first years, and VALife has a 2-year wait before full coverage. We can quote final expense so you can compare it with what VA offers.

Health coverage is a separate question from life insurance, and this page covers life insurance only. VA’s page on VA health care and other insurance (updated Nov 13, 2026) answers questions such as whether to sign up for Medicare at 65 when you have VA care.

Common questions

Life Insurance for Veterans FAQ

Should I keep VGLI or switch to private life insurance?
It depends on your age, your health and how long you need coverage. VGLI's monthly cost depends only on your age and the amount, and it goes up with each older age band. A private policy is priced on your health, age and tobacco use, so it can come out higher or lower. Keep your current coverage until any new policy is approved and in force. We quote both so you can compare.
What is VALife?
VALife is whole life insurance from the VA with guaranteed acceptance for veterans age 80 or under who have a service-connected disability rating. It offers up to $40,000 in $10,000 steps, with full coverage after a two-year waiting period.
Can I have VA life insurance and a private policy at the same time?
Yes. VA's own page on life insurance with preexisting conditions lists applying for both VGLI and a private policy as one option. We can quote term, whole life or final expense coverage to sit alongside what you have from VA.
How long do I have to apply for VGLI after I leave the military?
VA says to apply within 1 year and 120 days of leaving. If you apply within 240 days, you do not need to prove you are in good health. After 240 days, you need to send evidence that you are in good health.
Is Honorbrook affiliated with the VA?
No. Honorbrook Insurance is an independent agency and is not connected with or endorsed by the Department of Veterans Affairs or any government agency.
